title: Financial accounting and business basics for lawyers
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Read balance sheets, income statements and cash-flow statements, understand accrual accounting, compute ratios and the time value of money, and use the numbers behind contracts, damages, deals and valuation.
primary_reading: OpenStax: Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting

blocks.deliverable: Record ten transactions and balance the accounting equation.
Prepare both statements from a trial balance.
Reconcile net income with cash from operations.
Week 7 midterm; compute straight-line depreciation and a FIFO cost of goods sold.
Compute the present value of an annuity and of a lump sum.
Analyze a company's liquidity and leverage from its statements.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Deal memo: from supplied financial statements of a small business written for the course, compute key ratios and a present-value range for a proposed purchase, and write a 1,200-word memo on the legal and financial risks.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
